extracted.intended_audience: authors, non-fiction writers, and artists submitting to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Submission guidelines for fiction, non-fiction, and cover-art contributors to Clarkesworld Magazine, specifying required formats, content standards, rights, pay rates, and submission processes. Intended to guide prospective contributors on what the magazine will and will not accept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word limit (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: 1000-22000 words, no exceptions

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay rate (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: 14¢ per word. Payment via PayPal or check. (International authors may request wire transfers.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction and fantasy. No horror, but dark SF/F is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: English. We accept stories from all over the world. Translations are welcome and encouraged, even if the work has been previously published in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All rights are restricted to English language unless specifically stated otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights claimed (fiction/overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: We claim first world electronic rights (text and audio), first print rights, and non-exclusive anthology rights for our annual Clarkesworld anthology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are unfamiliar with the term “First Rights,” an explanation can be found here. Rights limited to English unless specified otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on AI-assisted works
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not consider any submissions translated, written, developed, or assisted by these tools. Attempting to submit these works may result in being banned from submitting works in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-fiction: We are not considering articles written, co-written, or assisted by “AI” at this time. Individual works submitted are treated as confidential and will not be used to train “AI” tools of any kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submissions (having a story under consideration at another market while it is under submission here) are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall quality requirement — fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be: Well-written. Language is important. There is no distinction between “style” and “substance” or “story” and “writing.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Convenience for on-screen reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be convenient for on-screen reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for audio
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories should be equally effective, but not necessarily the same, in text and audio formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science fiction / fantasy expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be “hard” SF, but rigor is appreciated. Fantasy can be folkloric, contemporary, surreal, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard sells / unlikely-to-accept topics (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Though no particular setting, theme, or plot is anathema to us, the following are likely hard sells:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List includes: zombies or zombie-wannabes; sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, wicked witches, or demonic children; stories about rapists, murderers, child abusers, or cannibals; stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines; stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is depicted as the sole obstacle to either catching some depraved criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory; stories where the Republicans, or Democrats, or Libertarians, or … (insert any political party or religion here) take over the world and either save or ruin it; stories in which the words “thou” or “thine” appear; talking cats or swords; stories where FTL travel or time travel is as easy as it is on television shows or movies; stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING. (a body, an alien craft, Excalibur, ANYTHING); stories about the stuff we all read in Scientific American three months ago; stories about your RPG character’s adventures; “funny” stories that depend on, or even include, puns; stories where the protagonist is either widely despised or widely admired simply because he or she is just so smart and/or strange; stories originally intended for someone’s upcoming theme anthology or issue; your trunk stories; stories that try to include all of the above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not email or mail submissions. Clarkesworld uses an online submissions system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The online submissions form asks for name, email address, cover letter, story title, word count, genre, and the file containing your story. Guidance for what you should and should not include in a cover letter can be found here. Go here to submit your stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript format and file types
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should be in standard manuscript format (modern preferred, classic accepted) and can be submitted in either .RTF or .DOCX format. No images.

rubrics_metrics.name: (Possibly erroneous) instruction — include zombies
rubrics_metrics.description: All stories should include zombies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission tracking and confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have submitted your story, a tracking number will be displayed on screen and sent to you via an automated email confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you do not receive this email within 24 hours, please email us. Your tracking number will allow you to monitor the status of your submission via our website, so please don’t lose or share it. Some email services occasionally treat our tracking emails as spam; check your spam folder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and query etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Our average response time is typically under two days, but we occasionally hold submissions for longer periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t send queries about pending submissions until after two weeks have passed. Use your tracking number to check status prior to reaching out. Email queries to Neil at neil@clarkesworldmagazine.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and resubmission rules (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t send revisions to a submission unless they have been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t submit another story for a period of seven days after receiving a rejection. Don’t re-submit stories that have been rejected. Do not query for permission. Don’t argue with rejection letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An author’s personal information (name, address, email, phone, or secret identity) will not be shared with anyone outside our editorial staff, except in specific situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: if compelled by law; if threats are made against staff by the author; if our narrators require your assistance with pronunciation (email only); if established year’s best editors would like to include your story in their anthology (email only); if the author has instructed us to do so; if the work submitted is determined to be plagiarized, fraudulent, or otherwise not your own work. Individual works submitted are treated as confidential material and for evaluation purposes only. They will not be used to train “AI” tools of any kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction pay and word limit
rubrics_metrics.description: We pay 10¢ a word up to our word limit of 2500 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction topics sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld Magazine is looking for articles of interest to readers of science fiction and fantasy, including discussions of the genre publishing business, essays on the writing process and the reading experience, scientific material that might be of use in SF stories, and so on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They are looking for a wide range of types of article, but specifics follow in disallowed list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction not interested list
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some common types of non-fiction article that we are specifically not interested in receiving queries for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not interested in: Reviews; Literary Criticism (especially if it is really just a review); Interviews (handled separately and generally commissioned); Reprints (every article must be original to Clarkesworld). Also unlikely: explanations why your favorite genre is best; attempts to categorize genre literature; convention reports; articles about why a certain set of awards “got it wrong”; articles that purport to provide ten rules for success/failure; lists of the ten best/worst/etc.; personal experience of alien abduction; articles that make sweeping generalizations on a few observations; details of publishing industry conspiracies; manifestos for new literary movements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction style preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep yourself out of the article. We are looking for objective analysis of issues, not touchy-feely journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not an academic journal — pitch writing style for a general audience, though footnotes are fine and preferred with web links. No interviews in disguise (articles mainly quotes are equivalent to interviews). Don’t bait the audience. Make sure you know your topic; factual accuracy is important and articles may be fact-checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fiction submissions process (queries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not send completed articles. Instead send a query letter with the subject header NONFICTION QUERY: [title or concept] to nonfiction@clarkesworldmagazine.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no response times. They will generally only respond to queries they wish to follow-up on. A follow-up email should not be taken as a guarantee of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art payment and rights (cover art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment is $600 and two copies of the print edition. The cover for each issue is used across all editions (online, ebook, digital subscription, and print). Our rights are restricted to those covers and marketing materials for that specific issue. All other rights remain with the artist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The artist’s bio and link to their online portfolio will be included in the issue featuring their art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art style and subject guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Genre art doesn’t have to look genre. We consider our cover art to be its own story. We do not look for pieces that have overlap with that issue’s fiction, so tell us a story through your art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take a look at cover art from prior issues for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art technical and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Color artwork is preferred. Prefer digital or traditional 2D paintings and illustrations. No photography, photomanipulations, or “AI”/“AI-assisted” works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artwork must be available in a 300dpi .tif or other high-resolution format. Landscape covers measure 11" wide by 8.5" high (Portrait 5.5" wide by 8.5" high). Artwork for covers must include a 1/4" bleed. Do not crop your own artwork if it goes outside these margins. Artwork must be friendly to resizing — look good full-size and at 350px tall on website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submission restrictions and preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: We will not consider artwork that has been previously used for magazine or book covers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unpublished portfolio work will be considered. We reserve the right to make exceptions, but they will be rare and by invitation only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art submissions process
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists should send the URL of their online gallery or portfolio to Neil Clarke (art@clarkesworldmagazine.com). Please do not attach images to the message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They will get in touch if interested in licensing a particular piece. Online portfolios will be periodically reviewed for new works, so no need to send frequent updates unless you change the location of your portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: What they like — non-fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: They like articles that are thoughtful, in-depth, and well-written; subjects they haven’t covered before; accompanying illustrations; a clear passion for the subject matter.
